tool.name: Bismark Deduplicate

param.name: mapping_output
param.label: Submit the resulting bam/sam file from Bismark bisulfite mapper

param.name: umi_mode
param.label: Use unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) found in the read names for deduplication?
param.help: Without UMIs, reads mapping to the same genomic position are considered duplicates. In UMI modes, reads must additionally share the same UMI.
param.option: No - deduplicate on genomic position only
Yes - UMI is the last ':'-separated field of the read name (e.g. MISEQ:...:CTCCTTAG)
Yes - UMI at an internal position of an Illumina bcl-convert read name (e.g. A00001:...:CAAGAG_1:N:0:AATGACGC)

param.name: umi_mismatches
param.label: Tolerate up to this many UMI mismatches
param.help: Reads whose UMIs differ by at most this many bases at the same position are treated as one molecule (UMI-tools directional rule). 0 requires exact UMI matches.

param.name: separate_logfile
param.label: Create a separate logfile, otherwise logs are added to the dataset info.

tool.help:
**What it does**
This tool removes alignments to the same position in the genome from the Bismark mapping output (both single and paired-end SAM/BAM files), which can arise by e.g. excessive PCR amplification. If sequences align to the same genomic position but on different strands they will be scored individually.
Note that deduplication is not recommended for RRBS-type experiments.
For single-end alignments only the start-coordinate of a read will be used for deduplication.
For paired-end alignments the start-coordinate of the first read and the end coordinate of the second read will be used for deduplication.
-----
**Deduplication with unique molecular identifiers (UMIs)**
If the reads carry unique molecular identifiers in their read names, deduplication can additionally key on the UMI, so that only reads mapping to the same genomic position *and* sharing the same UMI are treated as duplicates. Two UMI flavours are supported, depending on where the UMI sits in the read name (see the options above).
Optionally, up to a number of UMI mismatches (bismark >= 3.4.0) may be tolerated, so that reads whose UMIs differ by at most that many bases at the same position are still counted as one molecule.
